findings: Full interim results RNS (Investegate, 29 July 2026) with condensed financial statements — not slides-only or truncated (source: /workspace/docs/data/research_director_worker/BREE.L/20260904T182603Z/sources/filings/bodies/12bf5ad24805dc03.txt).
Group revenue +5% to £857.9m (H1 2025: £815.9m); +3% like-for-like. Underlying EBITDA broadly flat at £115.5m (H1 2025: £115.0m); +1% LFL. Underlying margin 13.5% vs 14.1% (−0.6ppt).
Statutory highlights: EBITDA £111.8m (H1 2025: £110.0m); PBT £26.7m vs £34.9m (−16%); statutory basic EPS 7.4p vs 8.0p. Underlying PBT £41.3m vs £48.9m; adjusted underlying basic EPS 9.4p vs 11.2p.

H1 vs FY2025 run-rate: H1 revenue £857.9m ≈ 50.1% of FY2025 £1,713.8m (guidance: 48:52 H1/H2 phasing). H1 underlying EBITDA £115.5m = 41.4% of FY2025 £278.8m. H1 underlying profit from operations £56.2m = 33.1% of FY2025 £169.7m.

Geographic mix (H1 2026 revenue / underlying EBITDA): GB £556.3m / £81.1m (flat rev, EBITDA −3%); Ireland £154.3m / £27.9m (+12% rev, +3% EBITDA); US £152.2m / £13.8m (+20% rev, +6% EBITDA, +14% LFL EBITDA).

GB: flat revenue and volumes/pricing; residential weakness — ready-mixed concrete volumes −8% vs H1 2025; aggregates/asphalt stabilising with infrastructure wins. Ireland: +12% revenue (+9% LFL); Kinnegad cement mill shutdown in May compressed margins. US: +13% LFL revenue, +14% LFL underlying EBITDA.
Group volumes: aggregates 15.0m t (+8%, +5% LFL); asphalt 2.0m (+6%); cement 0.9m (−3%); ready-mixed concrete 1.5m m³ (−3% reported, −6% LFL).

Cash flow: net cash from operating activities £21.4m (H1 2025: £10.8m). Net capex ex major projects £43.2m (H1 2025: £41.9m); PPE purchases per cash flow statement £46.2m. Free cash flow outflow £14.6m (H1 2025: −£25.0m). Acquisitions £106.9m cash.

Cash £80.1m at 30 Jun 2026 (H1 2025: £64.5m; 31 Dec 2025: £115.5m). Net debt (incl. IFRS 16) £690.5m (+7% vs H1 2025 £648.1m; vs 31 Dec 2025 £527.3m). Covenant leverage 2.1x vs H1 2025 2.2x (FY2025 LTM 1.8x); strong H2 cash generation expected to support deleveraging.

Interim dividend declared 5.00p (+5% vs H1 2025 4.75p); cash cost £17.4m; ex-div 1 Oct 2026, paid 6 Nov 2026. No dividend paid in H1 2026 period (H1 2025 paid £35.1m final). FY2026 total dividend cash cost guided £55m (all H2).

FY2026 guidance maintained: full-year underlying EBITDA in line with market expectations (consensus £280m, range £273m–£285m); capex £125m–£135m; revenue phasing 48:52 H1/H2; FY working capital outflow £20m–£30m. No explicit volume or margin targets.

GB outlook: construction demand expected to decline for a fifth consecutive year in 2026; continued residential new-build weakness; some infrastructure stabilisation but recovery timing unclear. Ireland and US outlook positive. Does not restate March “testing year” or April AGM trading-update wording.

Comparatives restated from 1 Jul 2025 to country-based structure (GB, Ireland, US); H1 2025 segmental figures restated on website. Cash/overdraft gross presentation restatement for 30 Jun 2025 comparatives (+£43.7m cash and current borrowings); no impact on net debt or covenants.
Acquisitions: Falling Springs completed 29 May 2026 (~£90m EV, £93.5m cash); Booth and Burfordville also completed; £110m capital deployed on bolt-ons in US and Ireland.
Back British Cement campaign referenced (launched March; policy asks for level playing field and carbon border measures).
Louis Eperjesi non-executive director appointment announced 29 Jul 2026, effective early 2027.
